<strong>Comprueba cada autovector.</stro: Check every eigenvector. Multiplying $Av$ and seeing whether $\lambda v$ comes out takes one line and catches the sign error in the characteristic polynomial, which is the commonest in the block.
<strong>En una cadena de Markov, comprue: In a Markov chain, check that the columns add up to one. If they do not, there is a transcription error and everything that follows will be wrong without showing it.
<strong>Los autovalores salen de un dete: Eigenvalues come from a determinant, and the determinant of a triangular matrix is the product of its diagonal. Before expanding, look at whether the matrix is already triangular or nearly so: it saves half a question.
<strong>Proyectar es restar lo perpendic: Projecting is subtracting the perpendicular part. Least squares, PCA and the projection onto a subspace are the same operation seen three ways; recognising that saves learning three formulas.
Cada tramo aporta un número fijo de preg: Each section contributes a fixed number of questions, drawn at random from its topics without repeating a topic while that is possible, and avoiding the most basic exercises. With 6 topics and 6 questions, one exam covers almost the whole block: that is why the link at the end reproduces the same exam, and “another exam” draws a different one.
Centrar datos y sacar la primera compone: Centring data and finding the first principal component; interpreting the singular values and truncating a decomposition; the transition matrix, the stationary distribution and where a chain ends up in the long run.
Cómo sacarle partido: How to get the most out of it
Decidir si unos vectores son base; matri: Deciding whether a set of vectors is a basis; the matrix of a linear map and a change of basis; the characteristic polynomial, eigenvalues and eigenvectors; diagonalising; projecting onto a subspace and fitting by least squares.
Diagonalizar es escribir la matriz en un: Diagonalising means writing the matrix in a basis of eigenvectors, and that needs three independent ones. With two you cannot get there, and the matrix only admits the Jordan form.
El enlace de un examen corregido reprodu: The link to a marked exam reproduces the same questions with the same numbers. A teacher can do one, copy the link and pass it to the class: everyone will sit the same exam and will be able to compare results and procedures.
Elige los tramos que entran. Las pregunt: Choose the sections to include. The questions are drawn at random from the exercises of each topic in the block, avoiding the most basic ones and without repeating a topic while possible. There are no hints: the marking and the step-by-step solution come on submitting.
Los autovalores se cuentan siempre con m: Eigenvalues are always counted with multiplicity, so that criterion distinguishes nothing. What decides is how many independent eigenvectors there are.
Los autovalores se llamaron primero <em>: Eigenvalues were first called Eigenwerte, “own values”, in Hilbert's German school, and they reached physics with quantum mechanics: the energy levels of an atom are the eigenvalues of an operator. The word travelled into English half-translated, with the first part left alone, and that is why everyone says eigenvalue today. Here they are computed by hand for the same reason derivatives are: to know what the computer is doing when it computes them.
No: harían falta tantos autovectores ind: No: as many independent eigenvectors as the multiplicity would be needed
Pasar a los complejos resuelve los autov: Going to the complex numbers solves eigenvalues that are not real, not a shortage of eigenvectors. Here the eigenvalue already exists: what is missing is one more eigendirection.
Seis temas que cuentan qué es de verdad: Six topics that say what a matrix really is: a map taking vectors to vectors, with directions of its own, with a way of fitting data and with a long-run behaviour. This topic teaches nothing new: it asks. A procedural exam with exercises from the whole block, with a clock and no hints.
Sí, pero solo sobre los complejos: Yes, but only over the complex numbers
Sí: basta con que haya tres autovalores: Yes: it is enough for there to be three eigenvalues counting multiplicities
Un examen de bloque es un simulacro hech: A block exam is a mock paper taken at home: with a clock, no notes and no hints. The questions come from the exercises of the 6 topics of the block, spread across sections, and every time you start one the numbers are different and so are the topics: doing it several times covers the whole block. On submission everything is marked, the step-by-step solution of each question opens, and the mark comes out section by section, with links to what is worth revising. The “tailored to what you have done” option puts first what you have not solved yet: it is the way to check that no topic is left untouched.
Una matriz $3 \\times 3$ tiene un autova: A $3 \times 3$ matrix has a repeated eigenvalue and only one independent eigenvector for it. Can it be diagonalised?
